title: Psalms Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 12.

questions.question: In Psalms 12, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth
They speak vanity every one with his neighbour
The LORD shall cut off all flattering lips
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1 begins with 'To the chief Musician upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David.' which appears first in the chapter.

questions.question: Who is the psalm addressed to in Psalms 12:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1 states, 'To the chief Musician upon Sheminith,' indicating it is addressed to the chief Musician.

questions.question: According to Psalms 12:1, why does the psalmist call for help from the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1 says 'Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men.'

questions.question: What do people speak according to Psalms 12:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:2 says, 'They speak vanity every one with his neighbour.'

questions.question: What kind of lips do people use according to Psalms 12:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:2 states, 'with flattering lips and with a double heart do they speak.'

questions.question: What kind of heart do the people have as described in Psalms 12:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:2 says, 'with flattering lips and with a double heart do they speak.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 12:3, what will the LORD cut off?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:3 states, 'The LORD shall cut off all flattering lips.'

questions.question: Besides flattering lips, what else will the LORD cut off according to Psalms 12:3?
options: The tongue that speaketh proud things
The feet that run to evil
questions.correctAnswer: The tongue that speaketh proud things
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:3 says, 'and the tongue that speaketh proud things.'

questions.question: Who ceaseth according to Psalms 12:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1 states, 'Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 12:1, who fail from among the children of men?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1 says, 'for the faithful fail from among the children of men.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 12:2, with whom do people speak vanity?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:2 states, 'They speak vanity every one with his neighbour.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 12:1 describes the psalm as being for the chief Musician upon Sheminith.
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1 states, 'To the chief Musician upon Sheminith,' confirming this fact.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 12:3 states that the LORD shall cut off the tongue that speaketh proud things.
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:3 says, 'The LORD shall cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that speaketh proud things.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 12:2 says that people speak truth with pure hearts.
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:2 states that people speak vanity with flattering lips and a double heart, not truth with pure hearts.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 12:1 says that the faithful are increasing among the children of men.
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1 says 'the faithful fail from among the children of men,' indicating they are not increasing.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 12:4, what do those who speak arrogantly claim about their tongue and lips?
options: With our tongue will we prevail; our lips are our own: who is lord over us?
Our words are pure and tested like silver
The LORD will cut off all flattering lips
The godly man ceaseth; the faithful fail
questions.correctAnswer: With our tongue will we prevail; our lips are our own: who is lord over us?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:4 states that those who speak arrogantly say, 'With our tongue will we prevail; our lips are our own: who is lord over us?' indicating their pride and defiance.

questions.question: What does Psalms 12:5 promise will happen if the LORD sees the oppression of the poor and the sighing of the needy?
options: He will arise and set them in safety from their oppressors
He will cut off flattering lips
He will purify His words like silver
questions.correctAnswer: He will arise and set them in safety from their oppressors
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:5 promises that for the oppression of the poor and the sighing of the needy, the LORD will arise and set them in safety from those who oppress them.

questions.question: How are the words of the LORD described in Psalms 12:6?
options: Pure words, like silver tried in a furnace, purified seven times
questions.correctAnswer: Pure words, like silver tried in a furnace, purified seven times
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:6 describes the words of the LORD as pure, compared to silver refined and purified seven times in a furnace.

questions.question: How does Psalms 12:5 relate to Psalms 12:4 in terms of God's response to human arrogance?
options: God will arise to protect the oppressed despite their arrogant claims
God endorses the arrogance of the lips in verse 4
God ignores the sighing of the needy
God cuts off the faithful from among men
questions.correctAnswer: God will arise to protect the oppressed despite their arrogant claims
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:5 follows the arrogant speech in verse 4 by promising that God will arise to defend the oppressed and needy, showing His opposition to their pride.

questions.question: What practical lesson can believers learn from the LORD’s promise in Psalms 12:5?
options: Trust God to protect and deliver those who suffer injustice
Speak arrogantly to prevail over others
Ignore the needy and their sighs
Rely solely on human strength for safety
questions.correctAnswer: Trust God to protect and deliver those who suffer injustice
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:5 encourages believers to trust that God will arise and protect the oppressed and needy, highlighting reliance on divine justice.

questions.question: Why might the purity of God’s words described in Psalms 12:6 be important for Christian living?
options: Because God’s pure words provide a trustworthy foundation for faith and obedience
Because pure words allow arrogance and pride to flourish
Because purity means God’s words are hidden and unclear
Because pure words encourage deceit and double hearts
questions.correctAnswer: Because God’s pure words provide a trustworthy foundation for faith and obedience
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:6 highlights the purity of God’s words, which assures believers that His promises and commands are trustworthy and worthy of obedience.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 12:4, how does arrogance manifest in speech?
options: By claiming control over one’s tongue and lips and defying authority
By speaking pure and tested words
questions.correctAnswer: By claiming control over one’s tongue and lips and defying authority
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:4 describes arrogant speakers as those who say, 'our lips are our own: who is lord over us?' showing defiance and self-will in speech.

questions.question: What does Psalms 12:6 suggest about the character of God's words compared to human speech in earlier verses?
options: God’s words are pure and refined, unlike the flattering and double-hearted human speech
God’s words are as vain as human speech
God’s words are arrogant and boastful
God’s words are silent and ineffective
questions.correctAnswer: God’s words are pure and refined, unlike the flattering and double-hearted human speech
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:6 contrasts the pure and refined words of the LORD with the flattering lips and double hearts described in earlier verses.

questions.question: What action does Psalms 12:3 say the LORD will take against those who speak proud and flattering words?
options: He shall cut off all flattering lips and the proud tongue
He will make their words pure
questions.correctAnswer: He shall cut off all flattering lips and the proud tongue
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:3 promises that the LORD will cut off flattering lips and proud tongues, showing His judgment against deceitful speech.

questions.question: How can Christians apply the message of Psalms 12:5 in their daily prayer life?
options: By praying for God to protect the oppressed and needy
By ignoring injustice and focusing on personal gain
By relying on human power to solve problems
By complaining about the arrogance of others
questions.correctAnswer: By praying for God to protect the oppressed and needy
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:5 encourages believers to pray with confidence that God will rise to protect those who suffer injustice.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'purified seven times' in Psalms 12:6 imply about the nature of God's words?
options: They are perfectly pure and trustworthy
questions.correctAnswer: They are perfectly pure and trustworthy
questions.explanation: The phrase 'purified seven times' in Psalms 12:6 symbolizes complete and perfect purity, emphasizing the trustworthiness of God’s words.

questions.question: How does Psalms 12:1 set the tone for the complaints found in the following verses?
options: It expresses a plea for help because godly and faithful people are disappearing
It praises the abundance of godly men
It describes a time of great peace and faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: It expresses a plea for help because godly and faithful people are disappearing
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1 opens with a cry for help because the godly man ceaseth and the faithful fail among men, framing the subsequent complaints about deception and arrogance.

questions.question: What practical behavior does Psalms 12:2 warn against among people?
options: Speaking vanity and using flattering lips with a double heart
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking vanity and using flattering lips with a double heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:2 warns that people speak vanity with flattering lips and double hearts, indicating deceitful and insincere speech.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 12:6 describes the words of the LORD as impure and unreliable.
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:6 explicitly describes the words of the LORD as pure, like silver refined seven times, indicating they are trustworthy and reliable.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 12:5 shows God's indifference to the plight of the oppressed and needy.
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:5 states that God will arise for the oppression of the poor and sighing of the needy, demonstrating His care and intervention.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 12.

questions.question: What does the Lord promise to do in Psalms 12:7?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 12:7 states, 'Thou shalt keep them, O LORD, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 12:8, what is the condition of the wicked?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 12:8 says, 'The wicked walk on every side, when the vilest men are exalted.'

questions.question: What shall happen to flattering lips according to Psalms 12:3?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Psalms 12:3 states, 'The LORD shall cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that speaketh proud things.'

questions.question: What does the Lord say He will do for the needy in Psalms 12:5?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 12:5 states, 'now will I arise, saith the LORD; I will set him in safety from him that puffeth at him.'

questions.question: What is described as pure in Psalms 12:6?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 12:6 states, 'The words of the LORD are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times.'

questions.question: In Psalms 12:2, what do people speak with their neighbors?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 12:2 states, 'They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: with flattering lips and with a double heart do they speak.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'צָרוּר' (tsarur) in Psalms 12:7 mean?
questions.explanation: This is correct because 'צָרוּר' (tsarur) conveys the meaning of protection or preservation, aligning with God's promise in Psalms 12:7.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Psalms 12:6 when describing the words of the Lord?
questions.explanation: This is correct because the verse compares the words of the Lord to silver refined in a furnace using the word 'as', indicating a simile.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God preserving His people as seen in Psalms 12:7?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 28:20 states, 'I am with you always, even unto the end of the world,' reflecting God's promise to preserve His people.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage reflects the wickedness described in Psalms 12:8?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Proverbs 4:19 states, 'The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble,' echoing the theme of wickedness.

questions.question: What precedes the statement in Psalms 12:7?
options: The words of the LORD are pure words
Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth
For the oppression of the poor
questions.correctAnswer: The words of the LORD are pure words
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 12:6 precedes Psalms 12:7, stating, 'The words of the LORD are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times.'

questions.question: What follows the declaration about the wicked in Psalms 12:8?
options: The LORD shall cut off all flattering lips
Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 12:8 concludes with, 'when the vilest men are exalted.'

questions.question: The phrase 'the faithful fail from among the children of men' in Psalms 12:1 indicates what about society?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 12:1 indicates a societal failure in faithfulness, suggesting corruption among the people.

questions.question: The statement 'Thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever' indicates God's eternal protection. Is this statement True?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 12:7 confirms God's promise of eternal preservation, affirming the statement.

questions.question: The phrase 'the vilest men are exalted' suggests a positive societal condition. Is this statement True?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 12:8 indicates a negative condition where wickedness is prominent, contradicting the statement.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 12:1 teach about the human condition in relation to godliness?
options: The godly man ceaseth and faithful fail among men, indicating a universal human depravity
Godliness is increasing among the children of men
Godly men are always preserved without fail
questions.correctAnswer: The godly man ceaseth and faithful fail among men, indicating a universal human depravity
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1 states 'for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men,' highlighting the doctrine that human faithfulness is not constant and that godliness can diminish in society, reflecting the fallen human condition.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sinfulness is taught in Psalms 12:2?
options: Humans often speak vanity with double hearts, illustrating the sinfulness of deceit and hypocrisy
Human speech is always truthful and sincere
Vanity speech is rare among the faithful
Double-hearted speech is a sign of divine inspiration
questions.correctAnswer: Humans often speak vanity with double hearts, illustrating the sinfulness of deceit and hypocrisy
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:2 says, 'They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: with flattering lips and with a double heart do they speak,' teaching the doctrine that human sinfulness often manifests in deceitful and hypocritical speech.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice is taught in Psalms 12:3?
options: The LORD will cut off all flattering lips and proud tongues, demonstrating God's righteous judgment against sin
God ignores human speech and does not judge it
Prideful speech is tolerated by God
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will cut off all flattering lips and proud tongues, demonstrating God's righteous judgment against sin
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:3 states, 'The LORD shall cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that speaketh proud things,' teaching the doctrine of God's active judgment against sinful pride and deceitful speech.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 12:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:6 describes 'The words of the LORD are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times,' demonstrating the divine attribute of purity in God's words.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 12:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:5 says, 'now will I arise, saith the LORD; I will set him in safety from him that puffeth at him,' demonstrating God's providential care and protection for the oppressed.

questions.question: How does Psalms 12:1-2 prepare for the New Testament theme of sanctification?
options: By illustrating the problem of pervasive human sinfulness, it sets the stage for the need of transformation by the Spirit
It shows human effort is sufficient for holiness
It denies the need for sanctification
It focuses exclusively on corporate worship
questions.correctAnswer: By illustrating the problem of pervasive human sinfulness, it sets the stage for the need of transformation by the Spirit
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1-2 highlights the scarcity of the faithful and prevalence of deceit, pointing to human inability to maintain holiness apart from divine sanctification, which aligns with New Testament teachings (e.g., Romans 8:13).

questions.question: In what way does Psalms 12:6-7 connect to the doctrine of Scripture's inerrancy and preservation?
options: It asserts that God's words are pure and preserved forever, supporting the doctrine of inerrancy and divine preservation
It claims Scripture is prone to error
It denies the lasting authority of God's word
It suggests human tradition is superior to Scripture
questions.correctAnswer: It asserts that God's words are pure and preserved forever, supporting the doctrine of inerrancy and divine preservation
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:6-7 states that God's words are 'pure words' and that the LORD 'shall preserve them from this generation for ever,' teaching the doctrine that Scripture is both inerrant and divinely preserved.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 12:3 and Psalms 12:5 teach about God's response to human sin and suffering?
options: God judges the proud and defends the oppressed, showing both justice and mercy
God only judges sin but offers no protection
God is indifferent to human pride
questions.correctAnswer: God judges the proud and defends the oppressed, showing both justice and mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:3 speaks of God cutting off proud tongues, while 12:5 shows God arising to protect the needy, together teaching God’s dual role in administering justice and mercy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 12:2 and Psalms 12:8 teach about societal corruption?
options: Corruption is widespread and involves deceitful speech and exaltation of the vilest men
Society is mostly righteous and just
Deceitful speech is rare and does not affect society
The vilest men are always punished swiftly
questions.correctAnswer: Corruption is widespread and involves deceitful speech and exaltation of the vilest men
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:2 notes deceitful speech, and 12:8 highlights wicked people walking freely and vilest men being exalted, together depicting a corrupt society.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 12:6 and Psalms 12:7 teach about the nature and preservation of God's promises?
options: God's words are pure and eternally preserved, guaranteeing the reliability of His promises
God's promises are conditional and often fail
God's words are impure and subject to change
God's promises depend on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God's words are pure and eternally preserved, guaranteeing the reliability of His promises
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:6 speaks of God's words being pure, and 12:7 affirms their preservation forever, together teaching the doctrine of God's faithful and immutable promises.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Psalms 12:6-7 is merely poetic and does not affirm the purity or preservation of God's word. What does Psalms 12:6-7 actually teach?
options: It teaches that God's words are pure as refined silver and are preserved forever, affirming their divine purity and preservation
It implies God's words are corruptible and temporary
It suggests human words are more trustworthy than God's
It denies any special status to God's words
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that God's words are pure as refined silver and are preserved forever, affirming their divine purity and preservation
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:6-7 clearly states 'The words of the LORD are pure words... Thou shalt keep them... preserve them from this generation for ever,' affirming divine purity and preservation.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 12:4 teach about human autonomy and divine sovereignty?
options: Human beings falsely claim autonomy over their speech and lives, denying God's sovereignty
Humans exercise true autonomous lordship over themselves
Divine sovereignty is limited by human will
Human speech is independent of divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Human beings falsely claim autonomy over their speech and lives, denying God's sovereignty
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:4 says, 'our lips are our own: who is lord over us?' illustrating human pride in autonomy, which is false when contrasted with God's sovereignty.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 12:7 regarding God's care for His people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:7 says 'Thou shalt keep them, O LORD, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever,' emphasizing God's attribute of preservation over His people and His word.

questions.question: How does Psalms 12:8 thematically connect to the prophetic critique of societal injustice in the Old Testament?
options: It portrays the prevalence of wickedness and the exaltation of vile men, echoing prophetic lament over social corruption
It praises the just leadership of Israel
It denies the existence of wickedness
It focuses exclusively on individual sin
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays the prevalence of wickedness and the exaltation of vile men, echoing prophetic lament over social corruption
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:8 states 'The wicked walk on every side, when the vilest men are exalted,' paralleling prophetic critiques such as those found in Isaiah and Amos regarding corrupt leadership and societal injustice.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 12:1 and Psalms 12:8 teach about the tension between godliness and societal wickedness?
options: Godliness declines while wickedness and the exaltation of vile men increase, illustrating the spiritual crisis in society
Society is neutral with regard to godliness
The wicked are always punished immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Godliness declines while wickedness and the exaltation of vile men increase, illustrating the spiritual crisis in society
questions.explanation: Psalms 12:1 laments the ceasing of godly men, and 12:8 notes the prevalence of wickedness and exaltation of vile men, together depicting a society in deep spiritual crisis.
